punchline: Napoleon told his messengers never to wake him for good news, only for bad.
thirty_sec: As a general, Napoleon had his secretary leave every letter unopened for three weeks. By the time he heard them, a lot of the 'urgent' problems had already solved themselves. Bad news was the exception: messengers had orders to wake him instantly. Ryan Holiday uses it as a model for filtering what reaches you, deciding up front what's allowed to interrupt.
